name: Value Lens Dividend Desk

answer_20pct.verdict: No Nifty 200 stock has a steady 20% yearly dividend yield over 10 years. The few that touched 20% in a single year did it through one-off special dividends or a price crash (flagged), not a repeatable payout. The honest best steady yields are about 5-9%. This report covers the Nifty 200 only; a few beaten-down micro/small-caps outside it can show very high trailing yields, but those are usually unsustainable, not a safe 10-year record.

portfolio.words: A sample Rs 600,000 income book for October 2026 in the steadiest high-yield Nifty 200 names (paid 8+ of 10 years, no reliance on special dividends). Buy at Monday's open; prices will differ from these closes.

score_method: Current yield (last 12 months' dividend / price), capped at 10% so a price crash cannot top the list — 40 points.
Consistency: how many of the last 10 years the stock paid a dividend — 30 points.
Steady, not one-off: full marks unless one year's payout was more than 2.5x the usual (a special dividend) — 20 points.
Growth: dividend higher than 10 years ago, or paid in 8+ years — 10 points.
limits: Dividend yield is not total return. A high yield often means the share price fell; check the price chart too.

Special one-off dividends are flagged (one year above 2.5x the usual); the flag targets single-year spikes, so a high-variance regular payer like a metals company can still look steady — read its 10-year bars.
Dividends are discretionary and can be cut, especially by cyclical and commodity companies.
Yahoo Finance dividend data can miss or misdate a payout; verify on the company page before buying.
Dividends are taxed at your income-tax slab. Paper research, not SEBI-registered advice.
